title: The counting block learns from an akien hand on the trouble's own record
intention: cairn/machines/counting_block teaches a who-writes-what row from the trouble lane's 'clears' verb (one increment per cleared_by entry whose hand_class is 'akien' on a who-writes-what-<triple> trouble), not from the journal caller class of the trouble file's write, which is always the trouble device's own process ('gate').
why: Akien 2026-10-10: "to the best of your ability, get it all closed", pre-approved through PROVED. Measured 2026-10-11 by cc0 after Akien ran ~/.akien/temp/clear-who-writes-what.sh (commons 9306593): all 9 clears landed in the trouble records as cleared_by {by: 'akien'}, but (1) the commons .artifact-journal.jsonl records every one of those 9 'clear' writes with caller class 'gate', because the write happens in the trouble device's process at the drain (cairn/devices/trouble/shim.py _fold, CLEAR_GATE), not in the clearer's; so cairn/machines/counting_block/block.py:164-176, which teaches a row only when the clear's journal caller class is 'akien', taught NO row: a read-only block.compile(block.read_journals()) on 2026-10-11 returns increments [] and every who-writes-what clear in the journal as disposition cleared:gate, so no clear has taught a row since the block was armed; and (2) every one stays standing OPEN, because its notified set is ['cc'] (DEFAULT_RECIPIENTS) and trouble.py clear() closes only when every notified recipient has cleared. The clearer's hand is lost at the emission: cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py clear_trouble emits {by, what_changed} and nothing measured; 'by' is a self-declared word.
traces_to: Law 6 (only Akien's hand teaches a who-writes-what row, ticket 5a4ec289bf15); RULE 1 (the trouble store is read through the trouble lane's interface); Law 3.
how: cairn/machines/counting_block/block.py only: replace the clear branch at :164-176 (pc == trouble_class and verb == 'clear') with a fold over the 'clears' answer: fetch it once per run over the bus (to='trouble', verb='clears', body={'prefix': IDENTITY_PREFIX}), and for each row with hand_class 'akien' increment slug_to_triple[row id]'s row; keep 'disposition' as 'cleared:<hand_class>'. The journal walk keeps counting raises exactly as today. If the trouble lane does not answer, the run reports increments as unknown (a loud field, not an empty list) and teaches nothing.
falsifier: cairn/machines/counting_block/proofs/test_an_akien_hand_teaches_the_row.py under PROVES {'0539e85f8b2d': {'1','2','3'}} with a fixture journal and a fixture clears answer: (1) a who-writes-what trouble with one cleared_by row of hand_class 'akien' adds 1 to its triple's row; (2) one with hand_class 'cc' (by 'akien') adds nothing; (3) the lane not answering yields increments 'unknown' and no row change. Hollow: reading the journal caller class again reds 1. Live check in the verdict: after Akien clears one who-writes-what trouble with c2172127d7a4 and 1c1b18bac2eb built, the row for its triple counts +1.

decisions.text: Read the trouble's own record of whose hand cleared it, through the lane's verb, rather than teaching the artifact journal about requesters: after 4ddc9df3369e the trouble store leaves the commons and its journal altogether, so a journal-based read would go blind anyway. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The clears verb (trouble.py _handle_clears, 1c1b18bac2eb) answers {'clears': [row, ...]} where each row is a dict with keys id, standing, by, hand_class, at; block.py reads row['id'] and row['hand_class'] by key, and hand_class is already case-folded ('unknown' when no hand). CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

compile(journals, rules=None, clears=None) takes the clears rows {id, standing, by, hand_class, at}. Each row is applied in time order (at parsed with datetime.fromisoformat) before the first journal entry whose at is later, so a raise before the clear gets its disposition and an entry after it is judged against the taught row; rows later than every entry are applied after the walk. A row sets disposition cleared:<hand_class> on every raise whose identity_slug equals its id and, for hand_class akien only, adds 1 to slug_to_triple[id]'s row and appends to increments. The journal clear branch at block.py:164-176 is deleted: a journal clear is counted as an ordinary write of its own triple, whatever its caller class. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
decisions.step: unlisted: Modify block.py compile() to fold clears instead of journal branch

decisions.text: pulse gains ask=None, a zero-argument callable returning a bus reply; None means reach('trouble').request(sender='counting_block', to='trouble', verb='clears', why=..., body={'prefix': IDENTITY_PREFIX}) from cairn.tools.bus_client, imported at call time (measured live 2026-10-11: 0.6s, 8 rows). It is called once per pulse and the rows are reply['body']['clears']. Any exception from ask: the fold runs with clears=[], the table's increments is the string 'unknown', and table['clears_error'] carries the exception type and text; nothing else changes. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
decisions.step: unlisted: Modify pulse() to fetch clears once per run, injectable

decisions.text: test_counting_block.py's World gains a clears list and World.pulse passes an ask returning {'body': {'clears': that list}}, so no World pulse reaches the live bus. Clause 3 keeps its journal clear entries and appends beside each one a clears row with the same id, hand_class akien or cc to match, and at equal to that journal entry's at; its assertions stand unchanged. The in-process CLI pulse of clause 4 keeps the default ask, because it is the live path. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The why passed to request() is the literal 'counting_block learns whose hand cleared each who-writes-what trouble (0539e85f8b2d)'; it is a required keyword of the bus request. IDENTITY_PREFIX is block.py:63's own module constant 'who-writes-what-', already defined there; nothing is imported for it. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

compile() returns a dict whose 'raises' list holds one dict per raised trouble with keys including 'identity_slug' and 'disposition' (initially 'raised'); a clears row whose id equals a raise's identity_slug sets that raise's disposition to 'cleared:<hand_class>'. 'increments' is a list of {clear, at, triple, count}, and 'rows' maps triple -> count; an akien row adds 1 to rows[triple]. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

pulse(roots, raiser, where, now, ask=None) calls (ask or _ask_clears)() exactly once, reads reply['body']['clears'] (missing reads as []), and passes that list to compile(read_journals(roots), clears=...). If the ask raises, compile runs with clears=[] and the table gets increments='unknown' and clears_error='<Type>: <text>'. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

Clause 3 is the tooth an_akien_clearance_teaches_the_row_and_a_cc_clearance_does_not in proofs/test_counting_block.py. The World fixture gains a clears list and a clear(slug, hand_class, why) method that appends the journal clear AND a clears row {id, standing:'CLEARED', by, hand_class, at}; World.pulse passes ask=lambda: {'body': {'clears': list(self.clears)}}. Clause 3's two journal clears become w.clear(...) calls; its assertions are unchanged. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

probes/raise_rate_falls.py: _measure carries table['increments'] as len() when it is a list and as the word 'unknown' otherwise (len('unknown') would read 7 increments), and _enough requires increments to be an int >= 1, so a pulse that could not reach the trouble lane never satisfies the probe. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

decisions.text: Today clause 3 writes each clear as w.append('CairnCommons', f'troubles/{block.slug(ident)}.json', 'clear', <hand>, <why>) — one journal entry, hand 'akien' then 'cc'. Each becomes w.clear(block.slug(ident), <hand>, <why>) with the same hand and why. World.clear(slug, hand_class, why) calls self.append(...) exactly as before and appends {'id': slug, 'standing': 'CLEARED', 'by': hand_class, 'hand_class': hand_class, 'at': self.t.isoformat(timespec='seconds')} to self.clears: 'by' is the hand_class argument and 'at' is the World's own clock, the same stamp the journal entry carries. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

_ask_clears() is a module-level function in block.py, defined just above pulse(): it imports reach from cairn.tools.bus_client inside the function and returns reach('trouble').request(sender=COMPONENT, to='trouble', verb='clears', why=<D4's literal>, body={'prefix': IDENTITY_PREFIX}). CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

World.clear(self, slug: str, hand_class: str, why: str) -> None; 'by' and 'hand_class' are both the hand_class argument, 'at' is self.t.isoformat(timespec='seconds'), 'id' is slug, 'standing' is 'CLEARED'. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
COMPONENT is block.py:55's existing module constant COMPONENT = 'counting_block'; _ask_clears uses it as sender and nothing new is defined. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
